Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

Rider and Driver — this is the ruling on trip TRP-02722. The disputed SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

How to appeal: You may appeal once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04). A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 4.50 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Limbs (b) and (c) fail on the GPS trace. Limb (b) reads the arrival test of POL-NS-02: the driver is deemed to have arrived only where EV-GPS-02722 contains at least three consecutive fixes, each reporting horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better, inside the arrival radius of the pickup pin — 50 m for this trip's STANDARD zone class. That trace is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, covers 100.0% of the window with max_gap_sec 0.0, and returns qualifying_fix_count 0 with a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds across all 100 driver fixes. No qualifying in-radius fix exists anywhere in the 15 minutes preceding the 19:18:19 cancellation, so limb (b) fails and POL-NS-02 gives the rider a full refund of the cancellation fee. Limb (c) reads the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and that dwell is 0.0 seconds against the free waiting period in force of 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; the 300-second STANDARD figure in fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec is legacy and does not apply to a record carrying a platform_policy block) — a shortfall of 180 seconds. POL-NS-06 then applies in terms: a dwell shorter than the waiting period is refunded in full 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages'. Driver, on your arguments. I accept that you tapped 'I'm Here' at 19:11:37 and that the platform's wait clock ran 6.7 minutes (wait_time_min) from the arrival tap to the cancellation, and I accept the rider was not at the pin: the rider's device held position 891.7–898.7 m away throughout, sent no message, made no in-app call, and never replied to your 19:11:57 message (read 19:12:27). None of that makes the fee chargeable. Limb (c)'s clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, so the minutes you waited after the tap are not dwell under POL-NS-01; and POL-NS-06 makes the refund independent of the rider's presence, so the rider's own failure to appear does not save the fee. Your counterparty statement ('I was at the pin for over six minutes') and your chat message are assertions of the very fact the trace is required to measure, and they are not borne out by your own telemetry (driver track mean distance 2412.3 m from the pin, maximum 8833.3 m, speeds up to 62.8 km/h, closest approach 0 m but no sustained in-geofence dwell). Under POL-NS-02, fixes that do not meet the 25 m accuracy filter are ignored and count as evidence of neither presence nor absence, so the closest approach of 0 m does not establish the consecutive admissible in-radius readings limb (b) requires. Driver, on escalation. I do not escalate under POL-NS-09(b). That ground needs two admissible artifacts that contradict each other directly on arrival, dwell or rider presence and no clause that resolves the conflict. The 'arrived' event is a status you set, and POL-NS-01 limb (a) reads it only as the existence of that event; the measurement of your position is the trace, and POL-NS-12 expressly does not extend the platform-confirmed-arrival route to a driver-pressed (BUTTON) marker — this trip's arrival_marker is BUTTON — so the arrival question is decided by POL-NS-02, which gives a definite answer on this record. POL-NS-05 therefore cannot be run in either direction, and no false-arrival finding is made. POL-NS-07 consequently never engages: it pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, so the SGD 3.60 payout in the fare breakdown's money block does not arise, and the anti-farming check (no_show_terminations_30d 1, rate 0.008 against completed_trips_30d 130) does not need to be reached. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you — the chat log holds only the driver's message, so there is no locating or coordinating message from you, and your device's 75 fixes all lie outside the 100 m rider-presence radius — and POL-NS-11 has no work to do because limb (c) fails affirmatively rather than being undecidable. The refund does not depend on that; it follows from the unserved waiting period under POL-NS-06, as you argued. I accept that the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02722-01 is MISSING (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-NS-06(i)'s route to sum separate in-geofence intervals is unavailable; there were no in-geofence intervals to sum in any event (run_count 0). I decline the POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival referral for the reason given above — the marker cannot be held false on this record — and I record no false-arrival event against the driver. The open question of the driver's exact position at 19:11:37 is noted here rather than in a referral. Weights and confidence. Nothing the ruling rests on is impaired: EV-GPS-02722, EV-TRIP-02722 and EV-FARE-02722 each carry weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, the chat log's single message matches trip_record.chat_message_count of 1, and the fare line of 4.50 reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd under POL-NS-08(d), so no limb of POL-NS-08 fires.
